# Hood squeak and rattle cures

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Spray WD-40 into the hood latch mechanism and apply silicon grease to the top of the hood bumpers. [t3217]

Apply adhesive-backed rubber pads to the contact points where hood cushion pads meet the body. [t3217]

[Partial] Untwist the hood bumpers and use electrical tape or felt pads. [t3217]

[Partial] Weld the hood shut to eliminate movement. [t3217]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Spray WD-40 into the hood latch mechanism.
2. Apply silicon grease to the top of the hood bumpers.

## Tools

## Parts

- Rubber pad: Almost looks like little pyramids [t3217]

## Tips & gotchas

- Space out the hood bumpers slightly to increase pressure on the hood. [t3217]
- [Partial] Use adhesive-backed rubber pads (foam circles with tape bottoms) where each bumper meets the body. [t3217]
- Use electrical tape on the latch loop for a final fix after other methods fail. [t3217]
- [Partial] Apply felt pads as an alternative to rubber pads, though they may wear out eventually. [t3217]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Using electrical tape alone without addressing other contact points first. [t3217]
